| [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) v4 | For a system driven without feedback through fixed kernels, the average work dissipated at each switch of the drive equals the memory that fails to predict the next input; that is nonnegative when the drive is Markov and, summed, bounds the protocol's dissipation from below when each kernel keeps its equilibrium stationary, so there only nonpredictive memory is wasteful; with feedback, in one binary channel no predictive agent is efficient | Still, Sivak, Bell & Crooks (2012), [LIT-327](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md): β⟨W_diss⟩ for the switch x_t → x_{t+1} equals I[s_t;x_t] − I[s_t;x_{t+1}] (Eq. 14, an identity). | [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v3 | For a memory evolving reversibly with its environment, Landauer's bound prices only steps that lose logical distinguishability, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit lost, exported to the environment and not necessarily as heat, so copying onto a blank register, measuring or evaluating a bit has no minimum cost; learning a label has a floor only in total entropy production, at least the information learnt, which in Goldt and Seifert's perceptron can be paid in the weights' own entropy with vanishing heat | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. The record derives it for a memory and environment evolving reversibly from an uncorrelated start: the environment's entropy rises by at least the logical entropy lost, H(X \| f(X)), and an injective step has no floor, attained exactly by a permutation. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) bound information learnt by total entropy production, payable with vanishing heat in their toy model. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. Whether the bound survives without reversible dynamics is [QUESTION-215](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-215.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) v4 | Organisms differ from dissipative structures such as a candle flame not by far-from-equilibrium self-maintenance, nor by circular self-maintenance alone, but by organisational differentiation: several distinct constraints that produce one another at different time scales | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Prigogine ([LIT-516](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-516.md)) supplies the dissipative structures, and nothing in his account separates them from organisms. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure, as Mossio and Bich (2014) already say of closure of constraints. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-128](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-128.md) | After mass bleaching, coral recovery on a reef crest depends on large herbivorous fishes keeping macroalgae down, because recovery runs through recruitment and survival that macroalgae suppress, not through the persistence of surviving colonies alone | Hughes et al. (2007), [LIT-711](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-711.md). On the reef crest at Orpheus Island after the 1998 bleaching, four roofless cages kept large and medium fishes out of 25 m² plots for 30 months. Macroalgae averaged 56% cover inside against 4.1% and 1.7% in controls. Coral cover reached 7.7% inside against 19.2% and 20.2%, with recruitment about two-thirds lower and mortality of established colonies more than double. Control recovery came mainly from recruits of taxa bleaching had removed. Proposed: one site, four replicates, plot scale, and fish exclusion standing in for herbivore exclusion. The algal state vanished within 30 days of reopening. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-129](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-129.md) | In Acropora millepora the natural night-light regime is necessary for spawning on the expected night, and displacing it delays or abolishes both release and a spawning-night programme of G-protein-coupled signalling genes | Kaniewska et al. | [THEORY-135](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-135.md) v2 | Multicellular cooperation depends on suppressing cells that gain fitness at the expense of the organism, across five foundations (proliferation inhibition, controlled cell death, division of labour, resource allocation and maintenance of the extracellular environment); cancer-like cheating on them is found across the independent origins of complex multicellularity, so complex multicellularity can be understood as a system for detecting and suppressing cheaters | Aktipis et al. | [THEORY-160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-160.md) v2 | In the algebraic Hamiltonian setting, symmetry and conservation correspond because the bracket is antisymmetric, which for a bilinear bracket is each observable conserving itself; the theorem's content lies in identifying observables with generators | Baez (2020), [LIT-819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-819.md), read in [NOTE-630](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-630.md), Theorems 3, 4, 8 and 10, with Alfsen and Shultz's theorem quoted as Theorem 12 and not checked here (QUESTION-142). | [THEORY-178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-178.md) v3 | In an ensemble of sign-consistent Boolean rules on the 87-gene core of E. coli's regulatory network, a transient knockout or overexpression of one gene can leave the network in a different attractor after release, and every gene that does so reaches a strongly connected component containing a positive circuit | Zhao, Wytock, Reynolds and Motter (2024), [LIT-854](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-854.md). | [THEORY-179](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-179.md) v2 | In Bhattacharyya et al.'s single-cell swarm assays of E. coli MG1655, the daughters of one mother swarmed alike at the fourth generation sampled and varied again at the seventh; swarm size correlated with a plasmid fepA-promoter reporter of Fur derepression by low iron (Spearman r = 0.71), and an iron chelator or added iron shifted swarming and held the shared state longer; a three-class switching model fitted to two time points matched the lineages only with a delay of three to four generations before switching, which the authors read as ruling out a bistable switch | Bhattacharyya et al. | [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md) v5 | On Monte Carlo samples of the 2D Ising model and of the 2D dimer model with added noise spins, a block coarse-graining trained to maximize mutual information with the system beyond a buffer recovered the variables renormalization already uses (Kadanoff block spins; the dimers' low-momentum electric fields, with no weight on the noise), and iterated on 128 × 128 Ising samples gave the flow away from the critical point, locating it to about 1% and giving ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, while a restricted Boltzmann machine trained by contrastive divergence on the noisy dimer data coupled to the noise and to columnar patterns instead | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md): shown numerically on two 2D lattice models whose relevant variables were known (Ising block spins, dimer electric fields), with an iterated Ising flow giving T_c to about 1% and ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, and analytically only for 1D and quasi-1D chains. | [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) v4 | Mehta and Schwab's correspondence between Kadanoff's variational renormalization group and restricted Boltzmann machines is an identity of parametrizations, under which an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution; away from that point it does not make training by distribution fitting a renormalization | Mehta and Schwab (2014), [LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md), Eqs. 18–22: setting the RG kernel T = −E + H makes the RG coarse Hamiltonian equal the RBM's hidden-marginal Hamiltonian for every parameter value, and Kadanoff's exactness condition equal to zero KL divergence. | [THEORY-202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-202.md) v3 | In variational renormalization over general Boltzmann machines, neither a matched partition function nor Kadanoff's exact trace condition makes a coarse-graining a renormalization: the first holds for joint Hamiltonians whose marginal is not the data, the second for hidden variables that do not interact with the system, so the variables a renormalization keeps must be fixed by a further stated condition | Lin and Tegmark (2016), [LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md), arXiv v1–v2 appendix, a part dropped from the journal text: a family of joint Hamiltonians with Z_tot = Z and the wrong marginal, and the remark that any non-interacting pair meets the trace condition. | [THEORY-205](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-205.md) v2 | For a short-range lattice model on a cylinder with a symmetric transfer matrix whose leading excited eigenvalue is non-degenerate, with block and environment as slabs L_B transfer steps apart, the uninformative information-bottleneck encoder first loses stability at β = (λ0/λ1)^(2L_B), in the direction of the boundary weak value of the leading excited eigenvector, which by the cited conformal finite-size relation is the lowest-dimension primary at large circumference; the uninformative encoder can stop being optimal at a smaller β, and nothing is shown for blocks inside a buffer shell or for the fixed-alphabet RSMI optimum | Gordon, Banerjee, Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2020), [LIT-885](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-885.md), Eqs. 3–5 and B2–C11, with one numerical check on a three-site critical Ising cylinder, reproduced exactly in [NOTE-690](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-690.md). | [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) v5 | In two optically trapped beads with a symmetric hydrodynamic coupling, one trap moved by a recorded noise drive, time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy follow the drive's path rather than the coupling's symmetry: the flow between the beads reads two-way under moderate drive, in experiment and numerics, and one-way under strong drive, in numerics of the fitted model only | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). | [THEORY-408](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-408.md) | In a one-locus model with non-overlapping generations, random mating and weak selection, gene frequencies change as if each individual maximized its inclusive fitness, so a trait that costs its bearer spreads only if its effect on relatives exceeds 1/r times the cost; the increase of mean inclusive fitness is proved only for traits whose total effect on others is not negative | Hamilton (1964), Part I, [LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md), read in full in [NOTE-401](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-401.md). Each effect an individual causes falls partly on genes identical by descent with its own (weight r) and partly on others, which only dilute. So selection tracks inclusive fitness. The threshold is written −k > 1/r (§5), not rb > c: "more than two brothers, or four half-brothers, or eight first cousins". | [THEORY-431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-431.md) | For classical systems with Markovian, microscopically reversible dynamics, the entropy production of a trajectory obeys an exact finite-time symmetry against the time-reversed process, P_F(+ω)/P_R(−ω) = e^ω, wherever ω is odd under reversal; Jarzynski's work equality and the mean second law follow as corollaries, and the symmetry constrains fluctuations, not which steady state a system selects | Crooks (1999), [LIT-522](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-522.md), read in [NOTE-413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-413.md), with Jarzynski (1997), [LIT-517](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-517.md) ([NOTE-417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-417.md)), and Seifert's review (2012), [LIT-523](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-523.md) ([NOTE-420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-420.md)). The work equality ⟨e^{−βW}⟩ = e^{−βΔF} holds at any switching rate, and Crooks derives it from a trajectory-level entropy-production theorem; Seifert derives every known theorem of the kind from one master theorem. These are exact given their premises. They are not proofs of the second law, since the dynamics build irreversibility in, and they say nothing about extremum principles for steady states. Their practical reach is work fluctuations of order k_BT. | Active |
| [THEORY-463](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-463.md) | In classical statistical mechanics a strictly irreversible approach to equilibrium cannot come from the isolated Hamiltonian dynamics alone: the fine-grained Gibbs entropy is constant and bounded systems recur, so each account surveyed either weakens the target to typical or long-run behaviour or adds something from outside the dynamics | Frigg & Werndl (2023), [LIT-114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md), the SEP entry, read in [NOTE-103](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-103.md). The impossibility half rests on standard consequences of Liouville's theorem, time-reversal invariance and Poincaré recurrence. The classification half is the survey's: it is stated account by account, not argued as a general result. The entry is classical only, excludes the direction of time, and reports rather than settles the disputes about each repair. | Active |
| [THEORY-466](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-466.md) | Among contestants of equal prowess with dangerous weapons, individual selection can favour conventional fighting backed by retaliation: an escalating Hawk is not evolutionarily stable, Retaliator is at most neutrally stable because Mouse ties it, and in a contest settled by persistence alone no fixed persistence is stable while an exponential mixture is | Maynard Smith & Price (1973), [LIT-505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-505.md), read in full in [NOTE-404](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-404.md). A simulation of five strategies, 2,000 contests per pairing, shows that "limited war" can be favoured by individual selection, without benefit to the species. The paper calls Retaliator an ESS "though Mouse does equally well", which fails its own second condition. There is no Hawk–Dove game, no "dove", no difference in prowess and no ownership, so it is not the source of display, deference or owner–intruder conventions. | Active |
| [THEORY-473](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-473.md) | Scaled down to one organism, Hutchinson's niche, defined as the conditions that give that individual an expected lifetime reproductive success of at least one, is observed only as a point; the rest of it is counterfactual, reached by translocation in only a few dimensions and otherwise inferred from other individuals, so in practice it is the niche of a phenotype class, and its authors call it mostly metaphorical | Takola & Schielzeth (2022), [LIT-127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-127.md), read in full in [NOTE-170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-170.md). The working definition (p. 5) gives the individualized niche an absolute-fitness boundary, expected LRS ≥ 1, and splits it into realized, potential, time-slice, prospective and trajectory-based niches. That the realized niche is a point and the potential niche unobservable follows from the definitions. The paper concedes there is "no empirical solution" at the individual level (p. 15), and its fix, marginalizing fitness functions across individuals, is schematic. It is a framework for structuring research, by its authors' own account, not a measurement. | Active |
| [THEORY-499](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-499.md) v2 | The breakup of the Eulalia parent body beside the Jupiter 3:1 resonance, 785–965 Myr ago, can plausibly have supplied the cluster of large lunar craters dated near 800 Ma, but shown only for the most favourable of five model solutions, the one carried through, with an average largest lunar impactor too small for Copernicus, and with the cluster's absolute date inherited from Copernicus alone | Bottke, Vokrouhlický, Dykhuis & Zellner (2026), [LIT-009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-009.md), read in full in [NOTE-002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-002.md). The Earth, Mars and Venus links are the authors' own speculation. Active as a reading of the model (ADR-065); whether the shower happened is THEORY-1195, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-508](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-508.md) | The Belousov–Zhabotinsky oscillation is a relaxation cycle in which autocatalytic production of HBrO₂ oxidizes the catalyst until bromide, released as the oxidized catalyst is reduced by bromomalonic acid, switches the autocatalysis off; a closed batch oscillates only as a transient of up to several thousand cycles on its way to equilibrium, and only a continuous-flow reactor sustains it indefinitely | Zhabotinsky (2007), [LIT-531](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-531.md), the Scholarpedia review by one of the reaction's eponyms, read in full in [NOTE-414](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-414.md). The mechanism is supported by the primary kinetics and by phase-resetting with injected Br⁻, Ag⁺ and Ce⁴⁺. The closed/open distinction matters for any use of BZ as a dissipative structure: a closed batch is a long transient, and only a fed reactor holds it away from equilibrium. The Oregonator models oscillation and excitability qualitatively, not quantitatively. The "several thousand cycles" figure is uncited, and the primary papers were not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-517](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-517.md) | Life raises the Earth's entropy production, chiefly by increasing the absorption of sunlight, and if the planet is held at maximum entropy production, the negative feedbacks of that state would give the homeostasis the Gaia hypothesis postulates | Kleidon (2009), [LIT-519](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-519.md), read in [NOTE-423](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-423.md). The Earth's entropy budget is dominated by the absorption of sunlight, and model studies, mostly the author's, find that biotic activity raises it. The step to Gaia is explicitly conditional on MEP, which the same review says is not established, and its feedback argument is a schematic figure. It treats life as the most effective of the Earth's dissipative processes, and gives no criterion separating a living dissipator from a convection cell. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-543](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-543.md) | Diffusion can destabilise a homogeneous steady state of reacting chemicals that is stable without it: a disturbance of one finite wave-length grows while uniform and very short ones decay, so a stationary pattern appears whose spacing is set by the reaction and diffusion constants and only its phase by the disturbance; with two substances this needs them to diffuse at different rates, and the pattern lasts only while free energy is supplied | Turing (1952), [LIT-535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-535.md), read in full in [NOTE-427](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-427.md), with Cross & Hohenberg (1993), [LIT-527](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-527.md), skimmed in [NOTE-418](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-418.md). The linear analysis on a ring gives exact conditions (9.4a, b) for stationary waves of finite wave-length; that equal diffusibilities cannot satisfy them is [NOTE-427](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-427.md)'s substitution, not stated in the paper. Turing calls the linearity assumption "a serious one" and the biological examples "very limited". Stationary chemical Turing patterns were first made in 1989–1991, and real morphogens implementing the mechanism had not been identified by 1993. | Active |
| [THEORY-562](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-562.md) | In REST2 replica-exchange simulations of intrinsically disordered proteins, high swap acceptance and short round trips show that replicas mix along the temperature ladder, not that conformations are sampled, because the upper rungs collapse the chain; sampling shows only when independent demultiplexed replicas agree in their structural distributions | Koneru, Reid & Robustelli (2025), [LIT-076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-076.md), read in full in [NOTE-076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-076.md). A how-to chapter whose one load-bearing methodological point is that high swap acceptance "is not, in isolation, sufficient evidence of robust conformational sampling or convergence" (p. 18). The reason the reading draws out is that REST2's upper rungs are unphysical Hamiltonians on which disordered chains over-collapse, so replicas can swap freely without the chain rearranging. The chapter argues this and shows a passing example; it shows no failed run, and its convergence criteria have no quantitative threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-567](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-567.md) | In the donation game, where a cooperator pays c for another to get b, defectors win in a well-mixed population, and each of five mechanisms makes cooperators evolutionarily stable above a benefit-to-cost threshold: kin selection r > c/b, direct reciprocity w > c/b, indirect reciprocity q > c/b, network reciprocity b/c > k and group selection b/c > 1 + n/m; the rules cover altruism only, not mutualism, coordination or conflict | Nowak (2006), [LIT-501](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-501.md), read in [NOTE-409](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-409.md), main text only. A four-page review that casts each known mechanism as a 2×2 game so that one set of criteria applies to all. The five ESS conditions are confirmed by the main text; the derivations are in the supporting material, which was not read, and in cited papers. Several rules hold only under weak selection, regular graphs or rare group splitting. Every mechanism is modelled with the donation game, so mutualism, coordination and conflict are outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-634](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-634.md) | In a ring of M chemotactic catalyst species, each making the next one's substrate, the non-reciprocal nearest-neighbour coupling makes the linear stability matrix circulant: the uniform state goes unstable for any M exactly when the species attract themselves, and the parity of M then decides the leading mode, a real alternating mode for even M that sorts species by parity into two static clusters, and a complex pair for odd M that can give persistent oscillation | Ouazan-Reboul, Agudo-Canalejo & Golestanian (2023), [LIT-036](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-036.md), read in [NOTE-079](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-079.md). The spectrum is exact for equal parameters (Eq. 5): instability iff μ(p) − μ(s) < 0, real leading eigenvalue for M = 2K, complex pair for M = 2K + 1. Brownian dynamics at M = 5 and 6 bear out the linear predictions; the odd-cycle oscillation is one trajectory at one parameter set. Direct metabolic partners repel; same-parity second neighbours co-aggregate. The origin-of-life reading is untested, and the authors concede in the review file that real catalysts' mobilities are unknown. | Active |
| [THEORY-655](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-655.md) v3 | Social behaviour evolves as if each individual valued a neighbour's fitness against its own by their coefficient of relationship, and its discriminations evolve to make that coefficient determinate; so kin are favoured and strangers met with hostility, relatives fight less, and haplodiploid sisters, related by 3/4, are predisposed to worker altruism | Hamilton (1964), Part II, [LIT-506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-506.md), read in full in [NOTE-410](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-410.md), on Part I's model ([LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md)). Two general principles, offered as an "unrigorous" generalization, are applied to alarm calls, kin recognition in gulls and terns, clones and colonies, Hymenoptera, and fights. The evidence is anecdotal. The author calls his positive indications for distant relatives "rather few and feeble", reports Australian halictines and multiple mating as running against the hymenopteran hypothesis, and explains anomalies case by case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-660](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-660.md) | The local branching geometry of physical tree networks, neurons, blood vessels, trees, corals and plants, is set by minimising the surface area of tubes that must keep a minimum circumference, not by minimising length: this predicts trifurcations once links are thick relative to their separation (χ = w/r above about 0.83) and orthogonal sprouts once one branch is much thinner than the other two (ρ = w′/w below about 0.6), both departures from Steiner trees that the data show qualitatively | Meng, Piazza, Both, Barzel & Barabási (2026), [LIT-069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-069.md), read in full with the SI in [NOTE-075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-075.md). Only two symmetric motifs are solved, each by a local, penalised optimiser started from the Steiner layout; the "exact" mapping to string worldsheets holds for a problem the paper does not solve. The random-terminal prediction is a sigmoid fitted to one tetrahedron, trifurcations are partly made by a merging rule, the one robustness check moves the key statistic 4.3-fold, and the sprouting breakpoints are chosen per dataset with no null. Real motifs are about 25% longer than Steiner, which the model leaves unexplained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-663](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-663.md) | Altruism between non-relatives can be selected when each act costs the giver less than it benefits the recipient, the same partners meet often and symmetrically, and help is withheld from those who do not return it; in humans, moralistic aggression, gratitude, sympathy and guilt are adaptations that regulate such exchange, and selection then favours sham versions of each and the ability to detect them | Trivers (1971), [LIT-510](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-510.md), read in full in [NOTE-402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-402.md). A verbal model, with a Prisoner's Dilemma sketch Hamilton communicated, followed by a functional account of the human emotions that would regulate reciprocity. The model is plausible and was later formalized. The psychology is fitted to 1960s social-psychology findings, mostly on American students, and the heritability of the dispositions is assumed. Trivers knows "of no psychological studies on the detection of sham moralistic aggression and sham guilt" (p. 51). His "unfairness" is inequity in exchange, not the division of a disputed resource. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-672.md) | In the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma with a probability w of meeting again, no strategy does better against an established TIT FOR TAT than TIT FOR TAT does against itself if and only if w ≥ (T−R)/(T−P) and w ≥ (T−R)/(R−S); always defecting is stable for every w, a cluster of reciprocators can invade it, and a nice stable strategy resists clusters, but the stability is only neutral, since always cooperating ties | Axelrod & Hamilton (1981), [LIT-498](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-498.md), read in full in [NOTE-411](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-411.md). Against TIT FOR TAT the best reply is always-defect or alternation, which gives the condition on w. The cluster result and the "ratchet" are explicit payoff comparisons. "Evolutionarily stable" here means no mutant does better, which is weaker than Maynard Smith and Price's definition: always cooperate does exactly as well. The model is deterministic and error-free. Tournament robustness is a separate, empirical claim about the strategies people submitted. | Active |
| [THEORY-679](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-679.md) | For dynamics obeying detailed balance in a heat bath, the heat released in a transition between observer-defined macrostates is bounded below by the log-odds against its reversal less the internal entropy change; where a replicator's likeliest way back is a copy decaying within one generation, the bound grows with the copy's durability and the speed of copying, not with the information copied | England (2012; J. Chem. Phys. 2013), [LIT-515](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-515.md), read in [NOTE-419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-419.md). The general bound, β⟨ΔQ⟩ + ln π(II→I) + ΔS_int ≥ 0, is a coarse-grained second law and was re-derived. Applied to replication it gives a heat cost of about 2n ln(n τ_decay/τ_div) per copy, which falls away as division slows. The numbers for E. coli (within a factor of three of the bound) and RNA rest on an upper bound on the reverse probability that is argued from biology, not proved, and on an internal-entropy term set "arbitrarily". It prices finite-time irreversibility, not information, and draws no line between living and non-living replicators. | Active |
| [THEORY-682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-682.md) | The time-average of a single threshold (Hill) response to a periodic signal is independent of the signal's period for a fixed waveform, so a frequency cannot be read by one sigmoidal stage; two cascaded stages can read it, because the first changes the waveform with period; and a delayed kinesin–dynein signalling loop whose period grows with axon length, read out this way and coupled to protrusion and contraction, can hold an axon at a stable length | Folz, Wettmann, Morigi & Kruse (2018; PRE 2019), [LIT-034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-034.md), read in full in [NOTE-067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-067.md). The period independence is proved, for signals that differ by a time rescaling only; the two-stage readout is shown numerically and in the Heaviside limit; the loop's minimum length and ω ≈ √3 v/L for long axons come from linear stability analysis. The length control is a lumped delay-differential model with one parameter set and the motor velocity v never stated, so its absolute lengths, about 125 µm, cannot be reproduced. A proof of mechanism, not a model fitted to axons. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-742](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-742.md) v2 | For a Boltzmann distribution linear in its couplings, observed through any coarse-graining map, the Fisher information the coarse data lose about the bare couplings is the expected conditional covariance of the energy operators given the coarse state; when the renormalized Hamiltonian stays in the family, the parameter map is linear and the additive constant of the step is analytic, that loss is the constant's Hessian, so the singular part of the metric passes unchanged to the coarse data. In the hopping model of diffusion at its Gaussian fixed point, keeping every n-th position of a trajectory of fixed duration multiplies the metric by n^(1−μ) in the μ-th Hermite coordinate: the drift's information is kept exactly, the variance's falls as 1/n, and higher shape parameters' faster | Raju, Machta and Sethna (2018), [LIT-1254](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1254.md), read in [NOTE-972](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-972.md). The loss identity holds for any coarse-graining of an exponential family; that the loss is analytic, and so spares the singular part of the metric, needs an exact renormalization step with linear beta functions and an analytic constant. It does not say that relevant directions keep their information in general: on the paper's own scalings only directions with RG eigenvalue above d/2 do, and away from the Gaussian fixed point even the drift loses information. | Active |
| [THEORY-747](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-747.md) | In Fourier–Galerkin large-eddy simulation, a first-order finite-memory Mori–Zwanzig closure tracks filtered-DNS energy decay and dissipation on the viscous Burgers equation and on the incompressible Taylor–Green vortex, isotropic turbulence and channel flow about as well as dynamic Smagorinsky where that model is at home and better than Smagorinsky and the t-model on the transitional Taylor–Green vortex; the memory length that fits it is set by the cutoff, not by the flow alone, scaling in Burgers roughly as 0.2 over the spectral radius of the resolved variables' Jacobian | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The closure is [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md)'s finite Markovian augmentation. Here is how it did, as far as the paper's plots show: close to filtered DNS in integral quantities, comparable to dynamic Smagorinsky in equilibrium turbulence, clearly better on a transitional flow, and with the subgrid transfer peaked at the cutoff where DNS puts it but about 40% too deep. The paper calls the predictions "excellent" with no numbers. Its fitted memory length shortens as the resolved dynamics speed up, so the memory belongs to the cutoff as much as to the flow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-748](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-748.md) | Block entropies, and so every lag-τ entropy rate of a stationary signal, are unchanged by the reflection x → −x and by time reversal, so they cannot detect the odd-order asymmetry the 4/5 law ties to energy flux; Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier's entropy rate conditioned on the sign of the increment breaks the reflection invariance, but h⁺ ≠ h⁻ shows only that the two-point distribution lacks central symmetry, which a skewed one-point distribution produces with exactly symmetric increments, so the test does not by itself detect skewed increments or an energy cascade | Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier (2016), [LIT-1243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1243.md), read in [NOTE-970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-970.md), claim that conditioning the entropy rate on the sign of the increment lets one "prove the existence of the energy cascade" using information theory. The record finds two limits. The unconditioned entropy rate is exactly blind to reflection and time reversal. The conditioned one detects any central asymmetry of the two-point law, including one with no increment skewness at all. Independent pairs with the paper's one-point skewness of 0.175 give h⁺ − h⁻ ≈ 0.066 nats with symmetric increments. Nothing in the paper ties an information quantity to the energy balance. | Active |
| [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) v3 | A weak solution of the incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box that lies in L³(0,T; B^α_{3,∞}) ∩ C([0,T]; L²) with α > 1/3 conserves kinetic energy, because the energy flux into scales below a mollification scale ε is bounded by Cε^(3α−1)∫‖u‖³ and so vanishes as ε → 0; this does not show that rougher solutions dissipate | Constantin, E and Titi (1994), [LIT-1248](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1248.md), read in [NOTE-982](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-982.md). The positive half of Onsager's conjecture, in the Besov form: if velocity increments obey ‖u(·+y) − u‖_{L³} ≤ C\|y\|^α with α > 1/3, integrated in time, the coarse-grained energy flux across scale ε is O(ε^(3α−1)) and no energy can be lost to vanishing scales. It is a statement about regular fields only. It does not show that a flux survives the limit for rougher ones: that energy can fail to be conserved below 1/3 is Isett's later theorem ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)), that it can strictly decrease is Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol's (THEORY-776), both Proposed, and some rough solutions conserve energy anyway. | Active |
| [THEORY-750](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-750.md) | For a stationary Gaussian signal the lag-τ entropy rate with one-point embedding is h_τ = H(X) + ½ log(1 − c(τ)²), so where the normalized second-order structure function 1 − c(τ) is small and scales as τ^ζ₂, h_τ = (ζ₂/2) log τ + constant; the "scaling of information" that Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier measure in near-Gaussian wind-tunnel turbulence, slope 1/3 in the inertial range and 1 in the dissipative range, is the scaling of the second-order structure function written in nats | Granero-Belinchón, Roux and Garnier (2016), [LIT-1243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1243.md), read in full in [NOTE-970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-970.md). A Gaussian identity and its small-lag asymptotics: the conditional entropy of x(t) given x(t − τ) is a monotone function of the autocorrelation, so its scaling exponent is half the structure-function exponent. In the Modane data the estimated entropy rate matches the Gaussian formula, so the measured "information spectrum" is S₂ again. It is not a distribution of a conserved quantity over scales, and it carries nothing about the direction or size of energy transfer. It answers [QUESTION-219](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-219.md) only in the narrow sense of supporting A3's caution. | Active |
| [THEORY-752](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-752.md) | In optimal prediction of a Hamiltonian system with separable energy and canonical initial law, projected by conditional expectation, the t-model's leading-order memory term tPLQLx makes the effective Hamiltonian of the resolved variables non-increasing, so the eliminated variables' memory enters as a damping that grows linearly in time | Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2002), [LIT-1253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1253.md), read in [NOTE-975](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-975.md): Theorem 8.1. Truncating the Mori–Zwanzig memory integral at its lag-zero value gives dΦ/dt = R̄(Φ) + tS(Φ), and under the stated conditions this dissipates the free energy of the resolved variables. It says nothing about how well the t-model predicts, gives no error bound, and holds only for the conditional-expectation projection; the true conditional mean's effective energy need not decrease. | Active |
| [THEORY-754](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-754.md) v2 | If a velocity field's third-order increments obey ‖δu(r)‖₃ ≤ C u_rms (r/L)^σ at every separation r, with 0 < σ < 1, then for a smooth, rapidly decaying filter the space-averaged energy flux across scale ℓ takes at most a fraction of order (ℓ/Δ)^(1−σ) from strain at scales above Δ and of order (δ/ℓ)^(2σ) from stress at scales below δ, measured against u_rms³/L·(ℓ/L)^(3σ−1); so transfer between scales is local in scale, with a power-law decay and no gap | Eyink and Aluie (2009), [LIT-1239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1239.md), read in [NOTE-969](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-969.md), stating bounds proved in Eyink (2005), [LIT-1252](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1252.md). A conditional inequality: if velocity increments scale no faster than r^σ in the L³ mean, the contributions of far larger and far smaller scales to the mean flux across ℓ are bounded by powers of the scale ratio. It needs 0 < σ < 1: σ < 1 for the large scales, σ > 0 for the small. That the inertial range satisfies the hypothesis, that the mean flux there is non-zero, and the sharper 4/3 exponent are assumptions or heuristics, not part of it. It is about one field decomposed by scale, and says nothing about units. | Active |
| [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md) | The finite-memory Mori–Zwanzig closure that Parish and Duraisamy take from Stinis, truncated at order m with one trapezoidal sub-interval and constant memory lengths, is a finite-dimensional Markovian augmentation: m + 1 auxiliary variables per resolved mode, each relaxing at rate 2/τ; at first order it replaces the memory integral by the kernel 2e^{−2s/τ₀} acting on the first-order term, which tends to τ₀ times that term, the t-model with t replaced by τ₀, when τ₀ is short against the resolved dynamics; its kernel is twice the true one at zero lag for every τ₀, so it is not exact even where the true memory is a single exponential, and nothing in the construction bounds its error | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The finite-memory closure turns the Mori–Zwanzig memory integral into auxiliary ordinary differential equations, so the reduced model is the resolved variables plus finitely many memory coordinates: the shape of augmentation [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) asks about. But the truncation drops the next auxiliary term without a bound, the memory length is fitted, and the kernel's form is fixed by the quadrature, not by the eliminated dynamics. It is an augmentation with uncontrolled error, not the controlled one the question asks for. | Active |
| [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) v2 | For every α < 1/3 there is a nonzero weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, with velocity Hölder-continuous of exponent α in space and time, that vanishes outside a finite time interval; its energy is not conserved, so the energy flux across a mollification scale ε does not vanish as ε → 0, and it runs in both directions, out of the vanishing scales while the energy rises and into them while it falls | Isett (2018), [LIT-1255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1255.md), skimmed in [NOTE-974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-974.md): the negative half of Onsager's conjecture. With [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) (Constantin, E and Titi, the positive half) it makes 1/3 the threshold. For the record, its point is that below 1/3 the energy flux into vanishing scales can survive the limit, which is the half of A3's point that THEORY-749 could not give. It does not say that this flux is a dissipative cascade. Isett's solutions start from rest, gain energy and lose it again, so the surviving flux takes both signs. Nor does it say that such solutions are limits of Navier–Stokes or describe turbulence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md) v2 | For every β < 1/3 there is a weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, in C⁰_t(B^β_{3,∞} ∩ L^{1/(1−3β)}), whose Duchon–Robert dissipation is the smooth nonnegative density E(t, x) = −e(t)e′(t)ρ₀(x₁, x₂)² fixed at the construction's first step; for such a solution the local coarse-grained energy flux into scales below ℓ converges, as ℓ → 0 and as a distribution in space and time, to E, so the transfer into vanishing scales is one-way at every place and time in the limit, nonzero inside a periodic array of pipes and zero outside them; where and how fast energy is dissipated is chosen by the construction, not forced by the equations, and nothing is shown about the sign at any positive scale | Giri, Kwon and Novack (2023; Annals 2026), [LIT-1289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1289.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1022.md): the L³-based strong Onsager theorem. Below 1/3, in Constantin, E and Titi's own scale of spaces ([THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)), there are weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality. In the proof the Duchon–Robert measure is a prescribed smooth function, positive in a periodic array of pipes and zero elsewhere. So the coarse-grained flux into vanishing scales is one-signed locally in space and time, in the limit, and not only for the whole box as in [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md). Its location and rate are inputs of the construction; it is a smooth density on a few pipes, not concentrated on a thin set; nothing is said about the sign at a positive scale or about vanishing viscosity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-774](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-774.md) | In a one-dimensional lattice hopping model with 2N+1 free hopping probabilities, all particles starting at the origin and the density after t steps observed with fixed Gaussian error, the Fisher metric is exactly t² times the distribution of the difference of two independent (t−1)-step walks, evaluated at the lag between the two hops, so it does not depend on the drift; when the walk is aperiodic with nonzero variance, its k-th largest eigenvalue is of order t^(3/2−k) for k = 0, …, 2N, so successive eigenvalues separate by a factor of order t | Machta, Chachra, Transtrum and Sethna (2013), [LIT-1299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1299.md), supplement §III, read in [NOTE-1018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1018.md). The eigenvalues grow for particle creation (t^(3/2)) and drift (t^(1/2)) and fall from the diffusion constant on (t^(−1/2), t^(−3/2), …). The data are not a coarse-graining of one fixed data set, so nothing forbids growth. The metric is a least-squares metric with an arbitrary unit of error, and its eigenvalues depend on the coordinates θ_μ. The ratio between successive eigenvalues matches the 1/n per Hermite order of [THEORY-742](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-742.md)'s diffusion result, though the two set-ups differ. | Active |
| [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md) v3 | For every β < 1/3 and every smooth, strictly positive and strictly decreasing energy profile e(t) on [0, T], there is a weak solution of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, Hölder-continuous of exponent β in space and time, with ∫\|v(t)\|² = e(t) at every time; for such a solution the energy flux across a mollification scale ε, integrated over any time interval, tends as ε → 0 to ½ times the drop in e, which is strictly negative, so energy leaves the resolved field for vanishing scales on every interval; this is one-way for the energy of the whole box, not at every point, and it is chosen by the prescribed profile, not forced by the equations | Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol (2017; CPAM 2019), [LIT-1300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1300.md), read in [NOTE-1013](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1013.md): the admissible version of Isett's negative half of Onsager's conjecture ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)). Any smooth positive energy profile can be imposed on a C^β solution, β < 1/3, so a strictly decreasing one gives solutions whose total energy only falls. Through [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)'s energy balance, the coarse-grained flux then runs into the vanishing scales on every time interval. That is the one-way transfer [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) could not give. It is one-way for the box as a whole, not at every point (no local energy inequality is proved); the same theorem gives increasing energy as readily, so the direction is a choice of the construction; and nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes, to a constant-flux inertial range or to uniqueness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-777](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-777.md) | In Monte Carlo on a 64×64 periodic square-lattice Ising model at its critical point, parametrized by a field and 13 nearby couplings and observed only through the spins left after n checkerboard decimations (b = √2 per step, n ≤ 6), the two Fisher eigenvalues along the field and the gradient of T_c stay within a factor of about two of their microscopic values, while the others fall by up to about six decades, in three groups whose decay is consistent with b^(2y−d) per step for y = 0, −2 and −4 | Machta, Chachra, Transtrum and Sethna (2013), [LIT-1299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1299.md), Fig. 3, read in [NOTE-1018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1018.md). One lattice size, one temperature, at most six steps of b = √2 (so b^n ≤ 8), no error bars, and no fitted rates. The groups and their rates are bands the authors drew. The value y = 0 is not an operator of the 2D Ising model: it is the rate at which any direction without singular support loses information as sites are discarded. The caption's rate 2^(−d−y) disagrees with the bands and with the supplement's b^(2y−d). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-780](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-780.md) | Transcriptional regulation alone can give a bacterium's gene expression a memory: in E. coli, a transient knockdown or overexpression of one regulator, with the environment held fixed, can leave other genes in a different self-maintaining expression state after it is released, as Zhao, Wytock, Reynolds and Motter predict from a Boolean-network model of its regulatory core | Zhao, Wytock, Reynolds and Motter (2024), [LIT-854](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-854.md), read in full in [NOTE-655](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-655.md). | [THEORY-821](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-821.md) | For every α < 1/15 there are weak solutions of the 3D incompressible Euler equations on the periodic box, Hölder-continuous of exponent α in space and time, that satisfy the local energy inequality; in the construction their dissipation measure is a nonnegative function of time alone, equal at each time to the rate at which the total energy falls, zero while the local energy equality holds and positive on all of space during a short final interval in which the solution's energy is drained to zero; uncountably many such solutions share one initial datum and one dissipation measure; for them the local coarse-grained energy flux into vanishing scales converges to that measure, so the transfer is one-way at every place and time in the limit and spread uniformly over the box, with its timing chosen by the construction, not forced by the equations | Isett (2017; ARMA 2022), [LIT-1305](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1305.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1027](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1027.md): the first continuous, indeed C^α with α < 1/15, weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality with nonzero dissipation, and a Cantor family of them sharing one initial datum and one dissipation measure. | [THEORY-1099](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1099.md) v2 | On Kay and colleagues' relaxed-clock dating of pre-LECA gene duplications, most duplications in eukaryotic gene families of archaeal origin, including actin, tubulin, vesicle-trafficking and nuclear-targeted families, predate the onset of duplications in genes of alphaproteobacterial origin at about 2.2 billion years ago, which the authors take as the start of mitochondrial endosymbiosis, so the host was elaborating its cytoskeleton, endomembranes and nuclear machinery before the mitochondrion; each date is a maximum age for its paralogues' functions, many intervals reach below 2.2 billion years, and the order of phagocytosis and the mitochondrion is left open | Kay et al. [THEORY-1101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1101.md), Active, holds what Tobiasson and colleagues find and conclude; whether the thesis holds is this entry's question, and its promote_when is [THEORY-1101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1101.md)'s old condition, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1203](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1203.md) | The host lineage elaborated its cytoskeleton, endomembrane system and nuclear machinery before mitochondrial endosymbiosis began, about 2.2 billion years ago: most pre-LECA duplications in eukaryotic gene families of archaeal origin predate it | The wider thesis Kay et al. assert, filed beside [THEORY-1099](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1099.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). | [THEORY-1205](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1205.md) | Eukaryotes began in a syntrophic partnership: an archaeal host fermented sugars and passed reducing equivalents to an alphaproteobacterial endosymbiont that contributed a TCA cycle and an electron transport chain, which is why the last eukaryotic common ancestor's central carbon metabolism is archaeal in cytosolic glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway and alphaproteobacterial in the mitochondrial TCA cycle | The wider thesis Santana-Molina, Williams, Snel & Spang assert, filed beside [THEORY-1109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1109.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). | [THEORY-1206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1206.md) | The mitochondrion was acquired late in eukaryogenesis, by a host whose proteome was already chimaeric, with genes from several bacterial sources acquired before it | The wider thesis Pittis & Gabaldón assert, filed beside [THEORY-1102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1102.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1).
